content:
【次世代LLMの革命！RWKVアーキテクチャが実現する長文推論と驚異のメモリ節約術】

今、AI界隈でめちゃくちゃ注目されている「RWKV（Recursive Key-Value Window）」という新時代のLLMアーキテクチャをご存知ですか？✨

これ、本当にすごくて、従来の「Transformer」と「RNN」の良いところをがっちゃんこした、ハイブリッドな仕組みなんです！

何が一番革命的かというと、文章が長くなっても「メモリを全然食わない」という点です！
通常のTransformerだと、文章が長くなればなるほど「KVキャッシュ（過去の会話内容などを一時的に記憶しておくメモリ）」がどんどん膨らんで、処理が重くなったりエラーになったりしちゃいますよね。
ところがRWKVは、独自の再帰的な仕組みによって、このメモリ消費をずーっと一定に保つことができるんです！数千トークンを超えるような超長文でも、推論スピードが全然落ちないのは本当に感動的ですね…！😭

さらに驚きなのがその効率性！

content:
【Ideogram 4で発生する「幽霊の手足」を防ぐ！高速モデルとLoRAの互換性対策】
最新の画像生成モデル「Ideogram 4」の高速版（Fastモデル）でLoRAを使ったら、なぜか不自然な手足（ゴースト肢）が映り込んでしまう……そんな現象に悩まされていませんか？🤔

実はこれ、モデルの「軽量化（量子化）」と「計算のブレ」が引き起こす技術的なミスマッチが原因なんです！

💡 何が起きているの？
「Fast」モデルは、処理をめちゃくちゃ速くするためにデータをギュッと圧縮（量子化）しています。でも、この圧縮によって細かい数値の精度（FP16からFP8などへの低下）が失われてしまうんです。
そこに特定の追加学習データ（LoRA）を重ねると、計算のズレが生じてしまい、本来ないはずのノイズが「謎の手足」として画面に現れてしまうんですね！さらに、GPUの計算順序のわずかな違い（非決定性）によって、出たり出なかったりする厄介な性質を持っています。

🛠️ 今日からできる回避策！
1️⃣ 複雑なLoRAを重ねる時は、圧倒的に高品質な「Original Dual Model」を使うのがおすすめ！
2️⃣ データの精度を保つために、LoRAの重みを圧縮せずに元の高精度（FP16など）のまま読み込ませてみる。
3️⃣ ポーズを制御する「ControlNet」の適用強度を少し抑えめに調整する。

速度を求める「Fast」と、クオリティを担保する「Original」を上手に使い分けて、ストレスのない創作ライフを送りましょう！✨

content:
【高解像度生成の革新！Nvidiaの「PID 1.5」でピクセル空間のノイズ除去を体験しよう！】
Nvidiaから、画像生成をさらに進化させる新しいアプローチ「PID（Pixel Denoising）1.5」が登場しました！✨

従来のStable Diffusionなどは、AIが処理しやすいように圧縮された「潜在空間（Latent Space）」でノイズを除去してから、最後にVAEというデコーダーを使って画像に戻していました。
ですが、このPIDはなんと直接「ピクセル空間（実際の画像データ）」でノイズを除去する画期的な技術なんです！

💡 注目したいメリット
・**早期終了（Early LDM termination）で超高解像度化！**
50ステップある拡散プロセスの途中（例えば44ステップ目）でピクセル空間での処理に切り替えることで、重いデコード処理を挟まずに最大4096x4096もの超高解像度生成を直接狙えます。
・**リアルな質感の向上！**
ピクセル単位で直接処理するため、お肌の質感や衣服の素材感といった細かいディテールが驚くほど鮮明に描写されます。 
・**既存のGPUでも動く互換性！**
DLSS5や最新のBlackwell世代のGPUを必須とせず、既存の環境でもソフトウェアとして動かせるのが嬉しいポイントですね！

⚠️ クリエイターとしての注意点
・**全体の整合性が崩れやすい**
高精細になる一方で、文字が歪んでしまったり、指先や顔の造形が不自然に崩れてしまう「アーティファクト（描写の乱れ）」が発生しやすい傾向にあります。
・**使いどころの見極めが大切**
すべての生成をPIDに任せるのではなく、質感にこだわりたい部分と、きっちりした構図を守りたい部分で使い分ける高度な検証が必要になりそうです。

現時点では「これだけで完璧！」というよりは、高解像度化のための頼もしい実験的ツールとして捉えるのがベスト。これからの進化がとっても楽しみな技術ですね！🚀

👉  https://t.co/goywtx9mWl
ドイツ語と英語で驚異的なパフォーマンスを発揮するオープンソース言語モデル「Soofi S 30B-A3B」がSoofi Consortiumからリリースされました！

総パラメータ数は31.6B（約316億）と大規模ですが、なんと推論時に実際に動く「アクティブパラメータ数」は1トークンあたりわずか3.2B（約32億）に抑えられています。この無駄のない「スパース（疎）設計」が本当にスマートですね！

技術的にも非常にユニークで、状態空間モデル「Mamba-2」と、特定の処理が得意な専門家を組み合わせる「MoE（Mixture of Experts）」、そして「GQA（グループ化クエリアテンション）」をハイブリッド化しています。

全52レイヤーのうち46レイヤーで「KVキャッシュ（推論を高速化するためのメモリ保持領域）」を使用しない設計になっているため、メモリの消費を劇的に抑えられます。長文の処理でも処理速度が落ちにくく、従来のモデルに比べてデコード速度が最大8〜9倍に向上することもあるなんて驚きです！

ドイツ語のデータ比率を従来の約5%から15.32%に引き上げたことで、ドイツ語のベンチマークでは70B（700億）クラスの巨大モデルを上回る素晴らしいスコアを叩き出しています。英語の性能もOlmo 3 32Bを超えるなど、両方の言語で圧倒的な強さを見せています。

NVIDIAの「Nemotron 3 Nano」の設計をベースにすることで、推論エンジン「vLLM」との互換性もばっちり確保されています。開発者がデータの影響だけを正しく評価できるよう配慮された、科学的な設計も素晴らしい工夫です。

Deutsche Telekomのインフラ上で訓練されており、データの透明性や安全性が重視されるビジネスシーンでも大活躍しそうですね！

He's not writing more code with AI. He's spending most of his tokens building and maintaining a personal knowledge base on whatever he's a
content:
Andrej Karpathy shared how he actually uses LLMs day to day:

He's not writing more code with AI. He's spending most of his tokens building and maintaining a personal knowledge base on whatever he's actively researching.

Here's the full breakdown:

1/ It starts with raw data ingestion. Web articles, research papers, GitHub repos, datasets, images. Everything gets dumped into a raw folder. He uses a clipboard tool and hotkey to capture sources fast without breaking his flow.

2/ An LLM reads, summarizes, and compiles all of it into a wiki. Not a messy notes folder. A structured collection of .md files with summaries, concept articles, and crosslinks between related ideas.

3/ Obsidian is the frontend and IDE. He views raw data, the organized wiki, and visualizations all in one place. The LLM writes and maintains the entire wiki. He rarely edits it directly.

4/ No RAG pipeline needed. Once the wiki grows big enough (around 100 articles, 400K words on a single topic), he just asks it questions. The LLM auto-maintains index files and reads its own index to find what it needs. No vector DB. No retrieval chain.

5/ Outputs go way beyond text. He has the LLM render markdown files, Marp slide decks, and matplotlib charts. Then everything gets filed back into the wiki as new articles.

6/ There's a self-improving loop built in. Every question he asks generates new content that feeds back into the knowledge base. The system gets smarter with every interaction.

7/ He runs linting passes as health checks. The LLM scans the wiki to find inconsistencies, fill gaps using web search, discover missing connections between articles, and suggest entirely new topics to cover.

8/ He vibe-coded extra tooling around it. A CLI, a search engine over the wiki, and a web UI. The search tool can be used directly in a browser or handed off to an LLM as a tool for larger queries.

9/ The wiki isn't static. It cleans itself over time. Every linting pass and every new query tightens the structure, fills blind spots, and strengthens the connections across the entire knowledge base.

10/ His next step is wild. Fine-tuning a model on synthetic data generated from his own wiki. So the knowledge lives in the model's weights permanently. Not just in the context window.

This is what separates using LLMs from building with them.

Most people treat AI as an answer machine. Karpathy turned it into a personal knowledge operating system. One system you can query, build on, and return to forever.

If you're deep in any AI or DL research topic right now, this workflow is worth stealing.

The court agreed with the lower court that New Jersey’s ban on Colt AR-15s is unconstitutional. It expanded the lower court’s order to reach the full class of semi-automatic rifles. The court also overruled the lower court’s ruling that upheld the state’s restriction on large capacity magazines, holding that the ban violates the Second Amendment. The majority reasoned that semi-automatic rifles and the magazines at issue are in common use for lawful purposes, and therefore fall within the Second Amendment’s protection. title: Rights group warns of increasing food insecurity in Afghanistan
content: Human Rights Watch on Friday warned of the deteriorating economic state in Afghanistan. Millions of citizens are at risk of suffering from severe hunger due to a sharp decline in international aid and restrictive Taliban policies that target women and hinder humanitarian access. Statistics from the United Nations warn that 46 percent of Afghanistan’s citizens will require humanitarian assistance in 2026. Over 17 million citizens out of a population of over 44 million are projected to experience food insecurity. In April 2026, only 20 percent of Afghanistan’s households were receiving an adequate amount of household food without assistance. As a result, Humanitarian organizations are relied upon. Funding shortfalls threaten the impact of humanitarian response. Reductions in foreign aid from the United States, which formerly funded up to 40 percent of Afghanistan’s Humanitarian aid, as well as reductions from the United Kingdom and other global donors, leave a jarring gap. Humanitarian organizations continue to be strained due to a high volume of need and limited resources. Throughout the country, millions of individuals are struggling with food insecurity, economic hardship, climate shocks , displacement, and individual protection risks. The funding for humanitarian responses is far below what is required to properly meet these needs. As of the end of May, the 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan had received just US$269 million against a requirement of US$1.71 billion. This leaves a funding gap of US$1.44 billion, marking a $110 million decrease compared with funding received at the same time in 2025, despite ongoing and growing needs across the country. Consequently, humanitarian groups are forced to reduce programming in order to triage with limited resources, leaving citizens needing additional support. Worsening the crisis, the Taliban’s policies create restrictions on women working within international aid organizations and the UN.

title: 20 states urge federal court to dismiss Trump administration suit over Jeffrey Clark bar discipline
content: A coalition of 20 state attorneys general on Friday urged a federal judge to dismiss a Trump administration lawsuit that seeks to halt disciplinary proceedings against Jeffrey Clark. Clark faces disbarment from his attempt to overturn the 2020 presidential election. In their brief, the officials argued that regulating state attorneys is a state police power under the Tenth Amendment . They also wrote that no government lawyer is exempt from professional-conduct rules. The coalition pointed to the McDade-Murtha Amendment, 28 U.S.C. § 530B, under which federal attorneys are subject to the ethics rules of their jurisdiction. They then highlighted the Younger abstention doctrine , under which federal courts generally refrain from interfering with pending state proceedings. Finally, the group warned that a ruling for the administration could immunize federal attorneys from discipline, regardless of their conduct. California Attorney General Rob Bonta said Justice Department lawyers should not “get special treatment” or be exempt from federal ethics requirements. The DOJ filed the suit on May 13 against the District of Columbia, its Court of Appeals, the Office of Disciplinary Counsel, the Board on Professional Responsibility, and disciplinary officials. It argued that the proceedings violate the Supremacy Clause and Article II of the Constitution by reaching internal executive-branch deliberations. The department framed the case as part of its campaign against the perceived “weaponization” of the legal system. title: UN rights expert demands justice for massacre of Honduran farmworkers
content: UN expert Morris Tidball-Binz on Friday condemned the killing of 20 Honduran farmworkers on the 21st of May 2026 and called for those responsible to be brought to justice, ensure that the victims’ families are provided with reparations, and that there will be no escalation of violence of a similar magnitude in the future. As the UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions, he also urged that the investigation adhere to the UN Minnesota Protocol , which governs the investigation of potentially unlawful deaths. Tidball-Binz further wrote, “[This tragedy] demands truth, justice and reparation … I reiterate my call on the national authorities and the international community to monitor compliance with these demands.” The killings took place on May 21 in Rigores, in the Bajo Aguán region of Colón department. Heavily armed men, some reportedly dressed in police uniforms, opened fire on oil palm plantation workers praying before starting work. The victims, which included women and children, allegedly held ties to a local peasant enterprise movement. The campesino network La Vía Campesina and the Catholic Church in Honduras condemned the massacre and demanded an impartial investigation . Additionally, the nation’s Jesuit order called for a UN-backed international commission of inquiry. They argued that the scale of the crime exceeded the capacity and will of national authorities, necessitating UN involvement. Honduran President Nasry Asfura condemned the massacre the following day, pledging that security and prosecutorial agencies would investigate. His government then ordered a military deployment to the area. On June 3rd, authorities announced the arrest of the attack’s alleged mastermind. The Bajo Aguán is contested by rival criminal groups fighting over drug-trafficking routes, though observers have questioned whether the killings arose from a gang dispute. title: EFF and ARTICLE 19 Submission to the European Commission on the DSA Trusted Flagger Guidelines
content: EFF and ARTICLE 19 have submitted joint comments to the European Commission on draft guidelines for the Digital Services Act’s trusted flagger mechanism. Having long advocated for a DSA that protects freedom of expression while preserving intermediary liability protections and the prohibition on general monitoring, we welcome the Commission's effort to provide practical guidance on how the trusted flagger system should operate. The DSA’s trusted flagger system can help platforms identify illegal content more efficiently. But if implemented poorly, it could also encourage over-removal of lawful speech, weaken due process, and give government authorities disproportionate influence over online expression. We support the Commission's focus on good practices and illustrative examples, rather than legal interpretations that could inadvertently steer platforms toward particular enforcement outcomes—and argue that the guidelines should include stronger safeguards to protect freedom of expression, due process, and the impartiality of the trusted flagger system. We also support the Commission's clarification that the DSA itself does not define "illegal content"; that determination must come from applicable national or EU law. Trusted flaggers submit prioritized notice, but platforms remain responsible for determining whether content is actually illegal. Platforms must therefore conduct careful, informed assessments and should not assume that a trusted flagger notice necessarily warrants restricting content. Our submission highlights several areas where the guidelines could be strengthened: Cross-border assessments require caution. Platforms should not rely on a trusted flagger notice to assess legality across Member States, where national legal frameworks may differ. Systemic risks extend beyond content moderation.
